hook: 'Water man of India' tells Telangana: don't copy *Sabarmati* for Musi
hook_b: 'Water man of India' tells Telangana: don't copy *Sabarmati* for Musi
tldr: At the Climate Conclave curtain raiser, Magsaysay awardee Rajendra Singh asked the government to build its own Musi model, keep banks green, and deny water to industries during El Nino.

beats.what: Rajendra Singh, speaking before the CM on Friday, advised against the Sabarmati model for Musi riverfront development.
beats.why: He cautioned against 'economic infrastructure' and 'contractor and corporate driven democracy', saying development should protect nature.
beats.care: He suggested bushes near the water, medium trees in the middle and tall trees above, and no concrete banks.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: He also asked the government to avoid commercial crops, deny water to industries during El Nino, not de-notify forests, and speed up HYDRAA's lake work. The government's response was not reported.

cards.q: Musi riverfront: which look do you prefer?

qs: What has the Musi plan proposed for the river banks so far?
How does Sabarmati differ from a natural riverbank?

facts.t: Singh said *15,800* small dams across those rivers were designed by local people, not engineers.

viz.verdict: Advice from one expert; no government decision reported.

viz.l: Small dams built by local people across his 33 rivers

cover.label: Small rivers he says he revived

insight: He asked for three layers of vegetation on the banks and no concretisation: 'Don't convert it into a canal.'

learn.t: Sabarmati model = Ahmedabad's riverfront with concrete embankments and promenades.

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.title: Water man of India Rajendra Singh advises against Sabarmati model for Musi river

fact: Rajendra Singh urged Telangana not to follow the *Sabarmati* model for the Musi
twist: He says he revived *33* small rivers without a single rupee from governments.
